answer: A willow survives the flood by bending, and an agent economy can do the same: require every agent to lock a bonded stake that cannot wander off before it earns trust. Reputation then accrues slowly, like a river carving its bed, through attested work over many epochs. An attacker may spawn a thousand names, but each needs its own stake and its own history, so forging a crowd costs as much as building one.
